chapters.title: The Pole and Foundation of Religion
editorial_queries: "the imams descended from the martyr" names no martyr, so the reader cannot tell which figure the lineage traces to.
comprehension_flags: The cyclical scheme — a messenger becoming "the seventh imam of that cycle" — assumes a doctrine of prophetic cycles that a general reader will not know and this pass cannot introduce.
terminology_notes: dawa — fix one spelling book-wide for the missionary enterprise, since it recurs and could drift to "da'wa"/"dawah".

chapters.title: By Nature and by Reason
terminology_notes: parenthetical transliterations (wujub, jibla, fitra, etc.) — the source carries these beside terms; a book-wide decision on whether to retain or strip them should be standardized, since this pass is not authorized to add or remove them.

chapters.title: Degrees of Excellence
terminology_notes: "gravity" (in "purity, radiance, and gravity") — rendered here as "weight"; standardize whichever of weight/heaviness/specific-weight the book uses elsewhere for this mineral property.

chapters.title: The Ladder of Creation
terminology_notes: imam — the source lowercases "imam" throughout while capitalizing pronouns for God is not in play here; confirm whether the book's house style capitalizes "Imam" so it is rendered the same way on every occurrence book-wide.

chapters.title: The Physician of Souls
terminology_notes: al-Hakim — appears once as "the Wise One (al-Hakim)" in [41] and once bracketed as "[al-Hakim]" apposed to "the Commander of the Faithful" in [39]; the two uses should be reconciled book-wide, since one names God and the other apparently names the imam.

chapters.title: Governance and the First Principle
terminology_notes: hudud — the source glosses it as "the ranks of the hierarchy"; this rendering should be standardized book-wide wherever the term recurs.

chapters.title: The Imam in the Pillars of Faith
terminology_notes: id feasts — should be standardized book-wide against however the book renders the two annual festivals (for example "Id" vs "Eid"), since it recurs across the zakat and khums passages.

chapters.title: God's Vicegerent in His Time
comprehension_flags: The numerical reckonings that call the Commander of the Faithful the sixth, seventh, ninth, and second at once — keyed to al-Muizz, al-Hakim, the four natures and five senses, and the start of each cycle — may leave a modern reader unable to follow how the same figure is counted several ways without help this pass is not authorized to add.
terminology_notes: qaim — left untransliterated-italic and lowercase here; confirm the book's standard casing/spelling for this term and for "vicegerent"/"vicegerency" across chapters.
